input:
Pervaporation separates a liquid mixture across a membrane under vacuum. The liquid feed contacts one side of the membrane, and vacuum on the other side draws the permeating component through as vapour. Two quantities describe performance, and both are stated per membrane as installed, on the feed as tested. Flux is the mass permeating per unit membrane area per hour (kg m-2 h-1). The separation factor is the water-to-alcohol ratio in the permeate divided by the same ratio in the feed, and is dimensionless.

A feed of 85 wt% isopropanol in water at 60 °C was tested on a polymer membrane and a zeolite membrane. One feed composition was tested, and no test ran beyond 500 h. The polymer membrane gave a flux of 1.6 kg m-2 h-1 with a separation factor of 180; its flux decreased 14% over 500 h. The zeolite membrane gave a flux of 1.1 kg m-2 h-1 with a separation factor of 320, and its flux was unchanged over 500 h within measurement error. Neither membrane leads on all three quantities. Rate favours the polymer membrane; selectivity and stability favour the zeolite membrane. Flux, selectivity and stability are seldom reported together for the same membrane, and this comparison is limited to the single feed composition and the duration tested.
